data.name: Shobharam
data.gender_notes: Shobharam is used as a male name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Shobharam means one who is radiant and beautiful. It is derived from the Sanskrit words shobhana (beautiful) and rama (pleasing). The name is often used to describe someone who is auspicious and elegant. The name Shobharam carries the meaning “Auspicious, Beautiful, Radiant” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Hindu tradition and is also used in Sanskrit, Hindi, Marathi. Parents who choose Shobharam usually hope their child will grow to embody auspicious, beautiful, radiant and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Shobharam is a name that evokes a sense of the divine. It is often used to describe someone who is beautiful in the eyes of God and radiates inner and outer beauty.
data.etymology: Shobharam belongs to the Hindu linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Auspicious, Beautiful, Radiant.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Shobharam total 4, giving a life-path number of 4. Number 4 is linked with Rahu and with the qualities of stability, discipline and hard work.

historical_references.reference: Shobharam was a renowned Hindu monk and philosopher who lived during the 13th century in India. He was a prominent figure in the Bhakti movement, which emphasized the devotional aspect of Hinduism. Shobharam is best known for his works on the philosophical concepts of love and devotion towards god, particularly Bhagavad Bhakti.

historical_references.reference: Another reference to Shobharam is found in the famous Indian epic, the Mahabharata. He is said to have lived during the period of the Kurukshetra war, around the 9th or 10th century BC.
